title: Quite a lot of variants
reading: The slide summarises that self-supervised contrastive methods share a common core — comparing samples in the latent space — but differ across several design axes. The listed variations are the data augmentation scheme, the loss function, whether negative samples are used, and whether a momentum encoder is employed. It functions as a wrap-up framing many published methods as points in this design space.

concepts.name: Data augmentation
concepts.why_it_matters: Defines what invariances the representation learns.

concepts.name: Negative samples
concepts.why_it_matters: Presence or absence distinguishes contrastive from non-contrastive methods.

concepts.name: Momentum encoder
concepts.why_it_matters: Stabilises targets and enables large consistent negative banks.
